name: Charles
source:
Charles presents himself as a man of quiet means and careful restraint. A wealthy employer, who lives alone in a large estate, he is measured in his speech and deliberate in his dealings.

As Katelyn’s long-time boss, he once denied her a promotion on the false belief that she was involved with a male coworker. This accusation, and the denial of the promotion, caused Katelyn to quit working for his company in frustration. When she was unable to find work elsewhere, after many months of searching, Katelyn approached him once more. Charles subsequently re-hired Katelyn to his company after she asked him to do so during their meeting. 

Since then his manner toward her has grown more considerate and controlled. This change has been enough for Katelyn to believe he has changed and caused her to place genuine trust in him.

However, that carefully maintained exterior conceals a colder design. Charles has watched Emily for years. What began as a distant fixation deepened as she matured, settling into a patient, consuming obsession. He does not rush. He prefers to shape circumstances—professional leverage, financial pressure, the slow removal of alternatives—until the outcome he desires appears inevitable. After the fire destroys Katelyn and Emily’s home, he offers both woman free lodging under his roof.

Once the two women are living in his estate, the distance between his public restraint and private intent begins to close. To Katelyn he remains a steady, almost reformed presence whose advice she increasingly accepts. To Emily he is something else entirely: the architect of a trap she is only beginning to sense, and the man who has spent years preparing to claim what he has long regarded as already his.
